scenes.name: hook
scenes.text: You try to screen record a movie on a streaming app, and all you get is a black screen. How does the app block it?

scenes.name: drm
scenes.text: It's called DRM, digital rights management. It's a set of locks that studios use so their videos can only be watched, not copied.

scenes.name: encrypt
scenes.text: The video arrives encrypted. Without the right key, the file is just useless scrambled data.

scenes.name: key
scenes.text: The app asks a licence server for a key, and only a trusted, checked device gets one.

scenes.name: secure
scenes.text: The video is decrypted inside a protected part of the chip, and sent straight to the screen on a secure path.

scenes.name: flag
scenes.text: The app also marks its window as secure. So the system's screen recorder and screenshot tools capture only black.

scenes.name: limits
scenes.text: It doesn't stop everything, like a camera pointed at the screen, but it makes easy copying much harder.

scenes.name: outro
scenes.text: Encrypt, license, decrypt securely, block capture. Follow for more on how things really work.
